title: Moving about
intro: Spanish is strict about direction in a way English is not. ir is away from here, venir towards the speaker, llevar is carrying away, traer carrying towards. Getting these backwards is the most persistent English-speaker error in the language.

entries.en: to come (towards me); to go (away from me)
entries.note: In English you can say I'm coming to your house. In Spanish that is voy a tu casa — you are going, because you are not yet there.

ex.en: I'm on my way over there.

entries.note: The same split as venir and ir. ¿Te traigo algo? offers to bring it to you here.

ex.en: Could you bring me a glass of water?

entries.en: to leave, to go out; to turn out

entries.note: Takes en or a, never a bare object: entrar en la casa, entrar al cuarto.

ex.en: We went in without making a noise.

entries.en: to go up, to climb; to get on (a vehicle); to raise

ex.en: We went up to the top floor.

ex.es: Sube al autobús, ya va a salir.
ex.en: Get on the bus, it's about to leave.

entries.en: to go down; to get off; to lower, to download

ex.en: We get off at the next stop.
I downloaded the app last night.

entries.note: Interchangeable with volver — see unit 1. regresar is commoner in Latin America.

ex.en: Move the chair over a bit.

ex.es: El gato saltó a la mesa.
ex.en: The cat jumped onto the table.

entries.en: to follow; to carry on, to keep doing
entries.note: seguir + gerund is the everyday way to say still doing something: sigue lloviendo, it's still raining.

ex.en: Follow me, I know the way.

entries.note: In Latin America pararse means to stand up; in Spain it means to stop oneself. A real difference.

ex.en: He stood up to greet us.

ex.es: No te muevas, ya casi termino.

entries.note: acercarse a. The opposite is alejarse de.

ex.en: She came closer to hear better.

ex.es: Cruza en la esquina, no aquí.
ex.en: Cross at the corner, not here.

entries.note: Usually reflexive for people: me caí. caerse bien means to get on well with someone.
viajar is to travel; el viajero the traveller. ¡Buen viaje!

ex.en: I'll wait for you at the stop.

entries.note: boleto in Latin America; el billete in Spain, where boleto means a lottery ticket.
hacer la maleta is to pack. el equipaje is luggage.
Plural aviones. volar is to fly; el vuelo the flight.
